header.running_head: The Encouragement the Sahabah (RA) Gave towards Seeking Knowledge

blocks.text: The Encouragement Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) gave Towards Knowledge

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA)
blocks.text: Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) both said, "Learning even a single chapter of knowledge is more beloved to me than a thousand Rakaahs of Nafl salaah." They also narrate that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "If death comes to someone studying the knowledge of Deen when he is still studying, he dies as a martyr." [^1]

Another narration states that they stated, "Learning even a single chapter of knowledge is more beloved to me than a thousand Rakaahs of Nafl salaah, regardless of whether the knowledge is practised upon or not." [^2]
The Encouragement Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) gave Towards Knowledge

Hadhrat Ali Azdi reports that when he once asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) about Jihaad, the Sahabi (RA) replied by saying, "Should I not tell you about something that is better than Jihaad? It is that you go to the Masjid and teach the Qur'aan, Fiqh or the Sunnah." [^3]

Hadhrat Ali Azdi reports that he once asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) about Jihaad. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) replied by saying, "Should I not tell you about something that is better than Jihaad? It is that you build a Masjid and then teach the Qur'aan, the Sunnah of Rasulullaah ﷺ and Deeni Fiqh." [^4]
Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "Everything seeks forgiveness for the one who teaches people what is good, even the fish in the oceans." [^5]
The Encouragement Hadhrat Safwaan bin Assaal (RA) gave Towards Knowledge

Hadhrat Zirr bin Hubaysh reports that when he went to Hadhrat Safwaan bin Assaal (RA) one morning, Hadhrat Safwaan (RA) asked, "What brings you here this morning, O Zirr?" "I have come in search of knowledge," Hadhrat Zirr replied. Hadhrat Safwaan (RA) remarked, "Begin your mornings as either an Aalim or a student of Deen, but never as anyone else." [^6]

Another narration states that Hadhrat Safwaan bin Assaal (RA) said, "Whoever leaves home in search of knowledge should know that the angels spread out their wings for the student and the Aalim of Deen." [^7]
